newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RESULTS TODAY-WEAK PRICES TO WEIGH AMPLATS.
newsitem.headline: RESULTS TODAY-WEAK PRICES TO WEIGH AMPLATS.

text.p: Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd (Amplats) was likely to report reduced earnings as a recent rally in Platinum Group Metals prices could prove too late to boost the company's results, analysts said.
Analysts said a rally in PGM prices -- which started late in May -- came too late to have any significant impact on Amplats' earnings for the year ended June 30.
And a strike at Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd (Rusplats) in May would also affect earnings at the world's largest platinum producer.
"The biggest contributing factor is the strike at Rustenburg," BOE Natwest analyst Paul Brogan said.
Analysts polled by Reuters predicted earnings per share for the year in a range of 165.0-186.0 cents with consensus at 174.0 cents from 190.3 the previous year.
They predicted a dividend of 122.5 cents/share from the previous 120.0 cents with a range of 120.0-125.0 cents.
Analysts said the results could be boosted by income from the company's diamond interests.
"I think the Amplats results could be bolstered from the diamonds which they may or may not want to show," said an analyst who asked not to be named.

"It should be good from the diamonds but they might not show it all because they obviously don't want to make the investor feel that the diamond interests were undervalued in the restructuring," he said.
Amplats said in April it was merging its three mines and the group into one listed company, using Rustenburg as the vehicle.
It said it would also dispose of its diamond interests to De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd and Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd for around 1.2 billion rand.

Amplats said the restructuring -- due to take place around September -- would allow it to focus on its core business of mining and marketing PGM metals, while at the same time helping it to move down the cost curve.

The company warned in February that it expected full-year earnings to be down on the previous year because dollar prices for platinum, palladium and rhodium had fallen markedly compared with the previous financial year.
Rustenburg was seen reporting earnings of 190.0-235.0 cents per share from last year's 314.4 cents
Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd could make 97.0-100.0 cents per share from 116.2 cents previously and Lebowa Platinums Ltd was seen earning 1.0-5.5 cents per share from 5.5 the previous year.
